quote: I will not be ‘famous’, ‘great’. I will go on adventuring, changing, opening my mind and my eyes, refusing to be stamped and stereotyped.
source: Virginia Woolf, A Writer’s Diary, the entry of 29 October 1933 (ed. Leonard Woolf, Hogarth Press, 1953)

evidence.where: A full scan of A Writer’s Diary read at the passage. The entry is headed Sunday, October 29th under the running year heading NINETEEN THIRTY-THREE, on page 213, and 29 October 1933 was indeed a Sunday. The sentences follow the paragraph on the philosophy of anonymity and are followed by The thing is to free one’s self: to let it find its dimensions, not be impeded. The volume carries Leonard Woolf’s signed preface and the Hogarth list of Woolf’s titles.
evidence.edition: A Writer’s Diary: Being Extracts from the Diary of Virginia Woolf, ed. Leonard Woolf (Hogarth Press, 1953)
evidence.locator: the entry of Sunday, 29 October 1933, p. 213

reason: Read in a scan of the book, not from a quotation site: the date, the wording and the punctuation all hold, including the comma and the stop placed outside the closed quotation marks in the British manner. The printing sets famous and great in double quotation marks; single ones are used here to match the house style of the other cards, which is typography and not wording. One thing for the editor: the Mrs Dalloway carry-in is also held for July, and only one Woolf may stand in a month.
